algorithms/ddmin.yaml.name: ddmin
algorithms/ddmin.yaml.problem: Find a small failing or interesting subset of change groups with an executable oracle.
algorithms/ddmin.yaml.input: Ordered reduction groups and an oracle returning PASS, FAIL, or INCONCLUSIVE.
algorithms/ddmin.yaml.output: A locally minimal selected set under the observed oracle.
algorithms/ddmin.yaml.algorithm: Test the full set, partition into complements and subsets, reduce granularity, and retry until no candidate passes.
algorithms/ddmin.yaml.complexity: O(n log n) oracle calls in the classic best case; worst case depends on inconclusive and non-monotone outcomes.
algorithms/ddmin.yaml.oracle_calls: Every candidate requires the configured executable verification path; cache keys must include repository and environment context.
algorithms/ddmin.yaml.termination: Stop when no partition candidate passes at maximum granularity or a configured budget is exhausted.
algorithms/ddmin.yaml.correctness_scope: Local minimality for a deterministic, monotone oracle; not global minimum and not semantic equivalence.
assumptions: candidate isolation
stable oracle
deterministic serialization
algorithms/ddmin.yaml.patchdiet_current_state: packages/core/src/reducer.ts implements a deterministic group reducer with cache and explicit INCONCLUSIVE state.
algorithms/ddmin.yaml.patchdiet_gap: No benchmark evidence yet compares the current search against classic ddmin on representative PatchDiet workloads.
algorithms/ddmin.yaml.recommended_use: Keep as the safety baseline and benchmark reference.
algorithms/ddmin.yaml.not_recommended_for: Automatic deletion without the executable oracle.

algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..name: hierarchical-delta-debugging
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..problem: Reduce structured changes at coarse and fine levels while preserving a valid oracle outcome.
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..input: A tree or hierarchy of change groups and executable oracle.
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..output: A reduced hierarchy whose removable nodes were accepted by the oracle.
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..algorithm: Reduce parent nodes first, then recursively reduce children that remain.
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..pseudocode:
reduce(node):
  if oracle(remove(node)) == PASS: return removed
  for child in children(node): reduce(child)
  return node
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..complexity: Depends on tree shape; avoids many combinations when hierarchy aligns with behavior.
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..oracle_calls: At least one per candidate node, plus retries for child reductions.
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..termination: Tree traversal ends when every retained node and descendant has been attempted or budget is exhausted.
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..correctness_scope: Local minimality in a chosen hierarchy; hierarchy can hide cross-branch combinations.
assumptions: meaningful parent-child grouping
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..patchdiet_current_state: AST and dependency groups exist, but reducer selection is not hierarchy-adaptive.
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..patchdiet_gap: No workload benchmark proves hierarchy reduces oracle calls without lowering removal precision.
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..recommended_use: Experiment after a benchmark fixture proves useful hierarchy.
algorithms/hierarchical-delta-debugging..not_recommended_for: Treating a hierarchy as proof of semantic independence.

algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.name: syntax-guided-reduction
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.problem: Avoid candidates that cannot be parsed or violate grammar-level invariants.
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.input: Parsed syntax tree or CST, reduction atoms, executable oracle.
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.output: Syntax-valid candidate patches accepted by the oracle.
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.algorithm: Choose removable syntax atoms, rebuild the source, reject parse-invalid candidates before oracle execution, then verify accepted candidates.
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.pseudocode:
for atom in syntax_atoms:
  candidate = rebuild_without(atom)
  if parse(candidate) has fatal errors: continue
  if oracle(candidate) == PASS: keep removal
return source
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.complexity: O(a * (parse_cost + oracle_cost)) for a atoms; oracle dominates when tests are expensive.
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.oracle_calls: One executable oracle call for each parse-valid candidate, with cache keyed by content and context.
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.termination: Atom list exhausted or budget reached.
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.correctness_scope: Syntax validity plus configured oracle outcome; no semantic equivalence guarantee.
assumptions: parser grammar
stable source reconstruction
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.patchdiet_current_state: Tree-sitter-related atomization and AST shrink files are present.
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.patchdiet_gap: Current workload evidence does not quantify parse filtering versus oracle overhead.
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.recommended_use: Keep as an opt-in candidate generator and benchmark.
algorithms/syntax-guided-reduction.yaml.not_recommended_for: Allowing parser success to bypass verification.

algorithms/weighted-delta-debugging.yaml.name: weighted-delta-debugging
algorithms/weighted-delta-debugging.yaml.problem: Try high-value or low-risk groups earlier when oracle calls have unequal expected value.
algorithms/weighted-delta-debugging.yaml.input: Groups with weights, executable oracle, deterministic tie-breaker.
algorithms/weighted-delta-debugging.yaml.output: Locally minimal selected groups under weighted ordering.
algorithms/weighted-delta-debugging.yaml.algorithm: Sort candidates by weight and feed the ordered sequence to a delta-debugging search.
algorithms/weighted-delta-debugging.yaml.pseudocode:
ordered = stable_sort(groups, descending_weight_then_id)
return ddmin(ordered, oracle)
algorithms/weighted-delta-debugging.yaml.complexity: Same asymptotic search as the underlying reducer plus sorting.
algorithms/weighted-delta-debugging.yaml.oracle_calls: Same candidates as baseline unless ordering improves early acceptance.
algorithms/weighted-delta-debugging.yaml.correctness_scope: Ordering affects search cost, not the oracle's authority or outcome.
assumptions: weights are advisory and deterministic
algorithms/weighted-delta-debugging.yaml.patchdiet_current_state: Feedback and risk evidence exist but are not an explicit reducer strategy.
algorithms/weighted-delta-debugging.yaml.patchdiet_gap: No measured relationship between current risk signals and removal precision.
algorithms/weighted-delta-debugging.yaml.recommended_use: Research-only ordering experiment with fixed baseline comparison.

algorithms/probabilistic-delta-debugging.name: probabilistic-delta-debugging
algorithms/probabilistic-delta-debugging.problem: Explore a large candidate space when deterministic ordering is too costly.
algorithms/probabilistic-delta-debugging.input: Candidate generator, random seed, oracle, budget.
algorithms/probabilistic-delta-debugging.output: A candidate accepted by the oracle and a reproducible trace.
algorithms/probabilistic-delta-debugging.algorithm: Sample candidate subsets according to a configured distribution and verify each sample.
algorithms/probabilistic-delta-debugging.pseudocode:
rng = seed(seed_value)
best = initial
repeat until budget:
  candidate = sample(best, rng)
  if oracle(candidate) == PASS: best = candidate
return best
algorithms/probabilistic-delta-debugging.oracle_calls: Bounded by the configured budget; every accepted candidate still needs verification.
algorithms/probabilistic-delta-debugging.correctness_scope: Empirical search result; no minimality guarantee and reproducibility requires recorded seed.
assumptions: randomness is isolated and traceable
algorithms/probabilistic-delta-debugging.patchdiet_current_state: No stochastic reducer is part of the runtime path.
algorithms/probabilistic-delta-debugging.patchdiet_gap: No evidence that stochastic search improves PatchDiet precision or cost.
algorithms/probabilistic-delta-debugging.not_recommended_for: Default CI cleanup or unrecorded deletion decisions.

algorithms/counter-based-delta-debugging.name: counter-based-delta-debugging
algorithms/counter-based-delta-debugging.problem: Use historical candidate outcomes to prioritize future combinations.
algorithms/counter-based-delta-debugging.input: Groups, outcome counters, executable oracle, deterministic policy.
algorithms/counter-based-delta-debugging.output: A reduction trace with counter updates.
algorithms/counter-based-delta-debugging.algorithm: Maintain per-group and pair counters; prioritize candidates with favorable observed outcomes, then verify.
algorithms/counter-based-delta-debugging.pseudocode:
counters = zeroed(groups)
while budget remains:
  candidate = choose_by_counters(counters)
  verdict = oracle(candidate)
  update(counters, candidate, verdict)
  if verdict == PASS: best = candidate
return best
algorithms/counter-based-delta-debugging.oracle_calls: One per selected candidate; all counters are advisory.
algorithms/counter-based-delta-debugging.correctness_scope: Empirical heuristic with no minimality guarantee.
assumptions: outcomes are informative across nearby candidates
algorithms/counter-based-delta-debugging.patchdiet_gap: No benchmark evidence for this workload.
algorithms/counter-based-delta-debugging.not_recommended_for: Replacing deterministic verification or claiming proof.

algorithms/program-slicing.yaml.name: program-slicing
algorithms/program-slicing.yaml.problem: Identify code relevant to a selected output, symbol, or behavior criterion.
algorithms/program-slicing.yaml.output: Forward or backward slice of nodes and edges.
algorithms/program-slicing.yaml.algorithm: Traverse dependency edges from the criterion in the chosen direction.
algorithms/program-slicing.yaml.pseudocode:
work = [criterion]
slice = {}
while work not empty:
  node = pop(work)
  if node in slice: continue
  add node to slice
  push unvisited dependency predecessors or successors
return slice
algorithms/program-slicing.yaml.complexity: O(V + E) for a materialized graph.
algorithms/program-slicing.yaml.oracle_calls: None for analysis; any removal still requires executable verification.
algorithms/program-slicing.yaml.termination: Graph traversal terminates on visited-node tracking.
algorithms/program-slicing.yaml.correctness_scope: Graph-relative relevance, not complete semantic dependence for dynamic languages.
assumptions: graph precision
criterion selection
algorithms/program-slicing.yaml.patchdiet_current_state: Lightweight symbol and dependency grouping provide partial relevance evidence.
algorithms/program-slicing.yaml.patchdiet_gap: Dynamic language and monorepo precision are not fully measured.
algorithms/program-slicing.yaml.recommended_use: Scope evidence and targeted test selection.

algorithms/change-impact-analysis.yaml.name: change-impact-analysis
algorithms/change-impact-analysis.yaml.problem: Estimate which tests, symbols, and files may be affected by a change.
algorithms/change-impact-analysis.yaml.output: Impact set for targeted verification and review routing.
algorithms/change-impact-analysis.yaml.algorithm: Map changed nodes into the dependency graph and traverse affected relationships.
algorithms/change-impact-analysis.yaml.pseudocode:
changed = map_diff_to_symbols(diff)
impact = closure(changed, dependency_edges)
return impact
algorithms/change-impact-analysis.yaml.oracle_calls: None for analysis; selected and full tests remain executable gates.
algorithms/change-impact-analysis.yaml.correctness_scope: Conservative only if graph is complete and edge semantics are sound.
assumptions: diff-to-symbol mapping
graph completeness
algorithms/change-impact-analysis.yaml.patchdiet_current_state: packages/evidence and packages/scope implement lightweight evidence and scope maps.
algorithms/change-impact-analysis.yaml.patchdiet_gap: No benchmark against optional SCIP import or hidden regressions.
algorithms/change-impact-analysis.yaml.recommended_use: Targeted-first verification with mandatory full verification.
algorithms/change-impact-analysis.yaml.not_recommended_for: Skipping required checks based on an incomplete impact set.

algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.name: regression-test-selection
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.problem: Select tests likely to exercise changed behavior while preserving a full verification fallback.
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.input: Change impact, coverage or mapping data, test inventory.
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.output: Ordered targeted test set plus required full suite.
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.algorithm: Map changed entities to tests, prioritize high-confidence candidates, then run the complete required verification before final status.
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.pseudocode:
targeted = rank_tests(map_change_to_tests(change, evidence))
run(targeted)
run(required_full_suite)
return targeted_results, full_results
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.complexity: O(mapping + test_count log test_count) after evidence exists.
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.oracle_calls: Targeted runs plus the mandatory full-suite run.
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.termination: Both targeted and full required commands complete or fail.
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.correctness_scope: Targeting optimizes search cost; only the required full suite supports final configured verification.
assumptions: test mapping is conservative
full suite is known
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.patchdiet_current_state: packages/core/src/targeted.ts and config test_selection support targeted-first execution.
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.patchdiet_gap: Hidden-regression rate needs benchmark evidence across real and synthetic fixtures.
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.recommended_use: Keep targeted-first behavior with explicit full-verification gate.
algorithms/regression-test-selection.yam.not_recommended_for: Labeling a candidate VERIFIED after targeted tests alone.

algorithms/mutation-testing.yaml.name: mutation-testing
algorithms/mutation-testing.yaml.problem: Audit whether tests detect representative behavior changes.
algorithms/mutation-testing.yaml.algorithm: Generate mutants, run configured tests, classify each outcome, and report confidence limits.

algorithms/mutation-testing.yaml.termination: Mutant inventory exhausted or research budget reached.
algorithms/mutation-testing.yaml.correctness_scope: Evidence about test sensitivity, not proof of semantic equivalence.
assumptions: repeatable tests
representative mutation operators

algorithms/mutation-testing.yaml.patchdiet_gap: No oracle-strength report connects surviving mutants to PatchDiet confidence wording.

algorithms/ast-differencing.yaml.name: ast-differencing
algorithms/ast-differencing.yaml.problem: Represent structural edits separately from textual line churn.
algorithms/ast-differencing.yaml.output: Insert, delete, update, move, and domain-specific refactoring evidence.
algorithms/ast-differencing.yaml.algorithm: Match nodes using stable labels and structure, then emit edit actions and confidence.
algorithms/ast-differencing.yaml.pseudocode:
old_tree = parse(old_source)
new_tree = parse(new_source)
matches = match(old_tree, new_tree)
return actions_from_unmatched_and_changed_nodes(matches)
algorithms/ast-differencing.yaml.complexity: Depends on matcher; typically superlinear in tree size for robust matching.
algorithms/ast-differencing.yaml.oracle_calls: None for analysis; candidates still require executable verification.
algorithms/ast-differencing.yaml.termination: Matcher terminates on finite trees and configured limits.
algorithms/ast-differencing.yaml.correctness_scope: Structural evidence and refactoring hypotheses, not semantic proof.
assumptions: compatible parsers
stable node identity heuristics
algorithms/ast-differencing.yaml.patchdiet_current_state: Diff and insight modules expose textual and lightweight structural evidence.
algorithms/ast-differencing.yaml.patchdiet_gap: No measured value for a JVM semantic-diff adapter on PatchDiet workloads.

limitations: implementation architecture is not scientific proof and repository license prevents casual code reuse
claims/program-reduction/claim-perses-00.possible_action: borrow concepts only; keep runtime dependency-free

claims/program-reduction/claim-creduce-0.statement: An explicit interestingness-test abstraction and isolated candidate execution make reduction passes composable and auditable.
assumptions: candidate worktrees or equivalent isolation are reliable
limitations: the reference targets C/C++ and its license state requires review
claims/program-reduction/claim-creduce-0.possible_action: preserve explicit oracle boundaries and candidate isolation

claims/program-reduction/claim-picire-00.statement: Complement testing, cache keys, and bounded parallelism can reduce wall-clock time for delta-debugging while preserving oracle decisions.
assumptions: oracle executions are isolated and deterministic enough for caching
limitations: parallelism can amplify resource pressure and nondeterminism
claims/program-reduction/claim-picire-00.possible_action: benchmark existing cache and worker pool before adding new strategies

claims/verification/claim-git-001.yaml.statement: Git patch output can include extended headers for modes, renames, copies, similarity, binary content, and quoted paths.
assumptions: Git output is the compatibility contract
limitations: a parser still needs fixtures for every format and merge-specific cases
claims/verification/claim-git-001.yaml.possible_action: retain round-trip fixtures for all documented headers

claims/verification/claim-git-002.yaml.statement: A combined diff describes a merge relative to multiple parents and cannot be treated as a sequence of independent two-way patches.
assumptions: PatchDiet accepts merge diffs or rejects them explicitly
limitations: current parser support must be verified with a fixture
claims/verification/claim-git-002.yaml.possible_action: document unsupported combined-diff behavior or add an explicit parse status

claims/verification/claim-git-003.yaml.statement: Git-compatible patch application validates patch context and file metadata but does not prove required behavior.
assumptions: Git is the application oracle
limitations: application success is necessary for patch fidelity but insufficient for correctness
claims/verification/claim-git-003.yaml.possible_action: keep patch application and configured tests as separate gates

claims/scope/claim-treesitter-001.yaml.statement: Incremental, error-tolerant syntax trees provide stable structural units for candidate grouping even when source is temporarily incomplete.
assumptions: grammar coverage and node ranges are trustworthy for the target language
limitations: error-tolerant parsing can create misleading structure; syntax evidence is not behavior evidence
claims/scope/claim-treesitter-001.yaml.possible_action: keep parser output advisory and require the oracle after every candidate

claims/scope/claim-scip-001.yaml.statement: A language-agnostic index can normalize symbol definitions and references across tools, but its value depends on indexer coverage and update cost.
assumptions: supported indexers are available in CI and Windows environments
limitations: protocol adoption alone does not improve precision; benchmark evidence is required
claims/scope/claim-scip-001.yaml.possible_action: prototype optional import and compare with SQLite graph

claims/testing/claim-mutation-001.yaml.statement: Mutation testing measures whether configured tests detect selected behavior changes through killed and survived mutants.
assumptions: mutants are isolated and tests are repeatable
limitations: mutation score is sample-dependent and equivalent mutants distort interpretation
claims/testing/claim-mutation-001.yaml.possible_action: use mutation mode to audit oracle strength in benchmark runs

claims/testing/claim-mutation-002.yaml.statement: Surviving mutants identify a verification confidence limitation, not permission to block or authorize cleanup by themselves.
assumptions: PatchDiet reports configured checks accurately
limitations: the audit cannot enumerate all untested behavior
claims/testing/claim-mutation-002.yaml.possible_action: surface WEAK_ORACLE evidence without changing deletion authority

claims/testing/claim-swebench-001.yaml.statement: Repository-level agent benchmarks are most useful when issue, base commit, patch, environment, and grading tests are recorded as one reproducible instance.
assumptions: container or equivalent environment is reproducible
limitations: agent repair success does not directly measure unnecessary-change removal
claims/testing/claim-swebench-001.yaml.possible_action: keep PatchDiet benchmark labels and validation gates separate from agent success rates

claims/review/claim-sarif-001.yaml.statement: SARIF provides a portable structure for tool findings, rules, locations, and artifacts that can support evidence transport.
assumptions: PatchDiet findings can map to SARIF result and location fields
limitations: serialization does not make findings correct or authorize removal
claims/review/claim-sarif-001.yaml.possible_action: prototype `--format sarif` only after mapping and consumer value are measured

claims/testing/claim-rts-001.yaml.statement: Change-based regression selection can reduce test work when its analysis is safe for the controlled program model.
assumptions: change and coverage mappings are complete enough for the model
limitations: PatchDiet repositories may violate model assumptions; full required verification remains mandatory
claims/testing/claim-rts-001.yaml.possible_action: use targeted tests for search and retain full-suite final gate

claims/review/claim-review-002.yaml.statement: Code review serves comprehension, knowledge transfer, and defect finding, so reducing unnecessary diff surface can lower review effort when evidence remains trustworthy.
assumptions: review effort can be measured with human or repository signals
limitations: study context predates current coding agents and does not prove PatchDiet impact
claims/review/claim-review-002.yaml.possible_action: benchmark human review effort separately from removal metrics

claims/review/claim-review-003.yaml.statement: Review-tool integration and lightweight workflows can scale review routing, but organizational case-study findings do not establish correctness.
assumptions: routing and review metadata are observable
limitations: Google's scale and tooling differ from PatchDiet deployments
claims/review/claim-review-003.yaml.possible_action: use as context for review routing experiments only

claims/review/claim-review-001.yaml.statement: Diff-filtered line annotations improve review routing but the transport layer cannot establish that a finding is correct.
assumptions: finding locations can be mapped to the current diff
limitations: line mapping and tool findings can both be wrong
claims/review/claim-review-001.yaml.possible_action: preserve evidence labels and human-review routing

claims/security/claim-security-001.yaml.statement: Secure development frameworks require documented provenance, protected build processes, and response practices around software changes.
assumptions: PatchDiet may run in CI over untrusted changes
limitations: SSDF controls are process guidance and do not replace sandboxing or tests
claims/security/claim-security-001.yaml.possible_action: retain provenance and runner isolation evidence in reports

claims/security/claim-security-002.yaml.statement: Monitoring runner process and network behavior can expose unexpected egress or supply-chain activity during untrusted verification.
assumptions: the CI environment exposes useful telemetry
limitations: monitoring is defense in depth and can miss activity
claims/security/claim-security-002.yaml.possible_action: research-only until a CI threat model and benchmark justify integration

claims/security/claim-security-003.yaml.statement: Heuristic supply-chain checks are evidence about project posture and cannot prove repository safety or patch correctness.
assumptions: scores are displayed with their evidence and scope
limitations: heuristics can be stale
incomplete
or misclassified
claims/security/claim-security-003.yaml.possible_action: keep as optional evidence, never a deletion gate
